feed.title: Mithlond watch
feed.subtitle: What's newly said about data centers and compute infrastructure in Hampton Roads, and by whom. Attribution over trust.

entry.title: Digest: 2026-11-20
entry.summary: Cardinal News reports that Roanoke City Council added a request for a two-year statewide data center moratorium to its 2027 legislative agenda. It is the only new item inside the watch's scope that could be opened today; it concerns Southwest Virginia, not Hampton Roads, and bears on the state-level rules that would govern data centers everywhere.

entry.title: Digest: 2026-11-18
entry.summary: The watch's first run: the past week, plus one catch-up on Hampton Roads. Virginia Mercury reports Gov. Spanberger and Democrats will propose local approval for data centers over 25 MW, while environmental groups call for a statewide pause. DatacenterDynamics reports Loudoun County adopted a moratorium of up to 12 months. At the Dominion–NextEra merger hearing, Dominion's counsel said the case isn't the place to decide whether data centers pay their fair share. WHRO reported in October that Suffolk paused data centers until it writes rules. Also tracked, and unrelated to data centers so far: Sen. Louise Lucas pleaded not guilty to federal charges (WTVR) in a case the U.S. Attorney's Office says concerns a marijuana enterprise.
